mesh_split.title: Your Thread network fell apart for {duration}

new_leader.title: Your Thread network had to reorganise itself

link.was_probably_leader: {border_router} was coordinating your Thread network. When the coordinator disappears, the other devices need a while to agree on a new one.
link.cause_unknown: No clear cause was recorded. Nothing was switched off and no bridge disappeared right before.
link.mesh_split: For {duration}, your Thread devices were split into separate groups that could not reach each other, until they agreed on a new coordinator.
link.new_leader: Your Thread devices had to choose a new coordinator. That took {duration}.
link.mesh_trouble_impact: During that time some devices did not respond, and adding a new device fails almost certainly.
link.pairing_failed_meanwhile: An attempt to add a device failed at the same time - very likely because of this.
link.border_router_gone_impact: Your Thread devices have one way less into your home network. If it was the last one, none of them can be reached.
link.border_router_on_switch: Every time {switch} was switched off, {border_router} disappeared shortly after – and came back once {switch} was on again. This happened {count} times.
link.border_router_on_switch_impact: Each time, your Thread network loses a bridge and may have to choose a new coordinator. Devices stop responding for a while, and adding devices fails in that time.
link.mesh_disturbed_during_pairing: Your Thread network was unsettled at exactly that time, so the new device could not be reached reliably.
link.pairing_stopped: The attempt stopped at this stage: {phase}.
link.pairing_failed_impact: The device is not part of Home Assistant. It may still believe it belongs somewhere and needs a reset before the next attempt.
link.weak_signal: {device} hears its nearest neighbour {neighbour} only faintly ({rssi} dBm).
link.weak_signal_impact: Commands arrive late or not at all, and the device may drop out now and then.
link.weak_signal_battery: Battery devices also run down faster, because they have to repeat themselves.
link.mesh_disturbed: Your Thread network was unsettled at that moment.
link.device_unreachable_impact: You cannot control it and its values are not updated.

origin.person_unknown: by someone in the Home Assistant app
origin.unknown: (directly on the device, or by something Home Assistant could not identify)

pairing.first_contact: The phone or Home Assistant could not start talking to the device. Usually it is too far away, not in pairing mode, or still paired elsewhere.
pairing.prepare: The device accepted the first contact but stopped responding while it was being set up. Usually the radio connection is poor at that spot.
pairing.authenticity: The device could not prove that it is a genuine certified product, or the certificate could not be checked.
pairing.keys: Handing the device the key to your home did not work. Often the device still holds keys from an earlier attempt.
pairing.network: The device could not join your Thread or Wi-Fi network. Often no router is close enough where the device is.
pairing.find_again: The device joined your network, but Home Assistant could not find it there afterwards. Usually the device is too far from the nearest Thread router or bridge.
pairing.finish: Everything was nearly done, but the last confirmation did not arrive.

fix.keep_border_router_powered: Plug {border_router} into an outlet that is always on, not into {switch}. It uses very little power when idle and your whole Thread network depends on it.
fix.check_border_router_power: Check that {border_router} has power and is connected to your network. Restarting it once usually helps.
fix.mesh_trouble_rare: Nothing to do if this happens rarely. If it happens often, check that your bridges (speakers, TV boxes, hubs) have power all the time.
fix.pairing_wait_for_mesh: Wait a minute until your network has settled, then try again.

pairing.first_contact: Hold the phone close to the device, put the device into pairing mode again, and check that it is not still added to another app.
pairing.prepare: Try again close to where the device will stay. If that fails, plug a Thread device that is always powered (for example a smart plug) in between.
pairing.authenticity: Update the device's firmware if the maker offers one. If it keeps failing, the device may not be certified for use outside the maker's app.
pairing.keys: Reset the device to factory settings before the next attempt.
pairing.network: Make sure a Thread router or bridge is nearby - for example a smart plug or a speaker - or bring the device closer for pairing.
pairing.find_again: Pair the device closer to a bridge or an always-powered Thread device. Once added, you can move it back.
pairing.finish: Check whether the device appeared in Home Assistant after all. If not, reset it and try again.

fix.pairing_reset_and_retry: Before trying again: reset the device to factory settings, then scan the code again.
fix.weak_signal: Put a Thread device that is always powered (for example a smart plug) between {device} and {neighbour}, or move {device} a little closer.
fix.device_unreachable: Check that {device} has power - or fresh batteries. If it runs on batteries, take them out for ten seconds and put them back.
